assessment: Directly addresses CATO sensitivity request. Main numerical observations reproduced on the saved sample; narrative claims of cause, permanence and precise volatility attribution remain stronger than evidence.
verified: See checks.json and check.py: top10 trim; 21/42/63/126 correlations; nine 21-session blocks; SPY betas; SPY partial correlation; annualized return/gap volatility; overlapping-window persistence check. Earlier identical-sample R2 correction remains confirmed.
limits: Saved same-vendor data; historical coverage differs (3666 vs 3708 63-session windows). No report scripts, issuer NAV series or extended ETF/constituent panels supplied.

findings.claim: Low correlation precedes the September/October events
findings.detail: June block 0.677 and July 0.640 reproduced. Persistence observed to October 30 does not establish future permanence.

findings.claim: SPY control makes bank-pair relationship less unusual
findings.detail: Current partial correlation 0.72765; matched historical median 0.87492 and percentile 10.37 on our shorter history, versus reported 11.1. Raw correlation only rises from 0.719 to 0.728; rarity changes because historical benchmark changes too. Not a causal allocation or proof that bank-specific differences vanish.

findings.claim: Half the correlation decline is the Forbes-Rigobon effect
findings.detail: The variance identity is correct, but plugging in marginal medians is not a unique decomposition. Uniform scaling of returns leaves correlation unchanged. Volatility-dependent correlation requires assumptions about common versus idiosyncratic shocks. The cited paper explicitly requires assumptions for adjustment.
R2 values are wrong for the stated single-factor sample. Candidate fits such as degrees-of-freedom mismatch do not establish the actual coding history or prove multiple methods were used.

findings.claim: 99.5% historical reversion implies expected reversion now
findings.detail: Approximately reproduced as 1/175 qualifying overlapping windows remaining below 0.863 after 63 sessions. These are dependent conditioning windows, not 175 separate episodes; selection and retrospective threshold remain.

findings.claim: Lower-frequency and NAV checks rule out artifacts
findings.detail: Reported checks weaken simple stale-close or ETF-pricing explanations, but do not eliminate every microstructure effect. Lower-frequency checks also extend the lookback to 126 sessions. NAV and extended panels not independently replicated.

findings.claim: Constituent comparisons identify a size mechanism
findings.detail: Current-member survivorship bias disclosed. Common factors, holdings overlap and compositional choices prevent causal attribution to size alone.
September 2026 issuer factsheet states linked KBW Regional Banking Index to October 24, 2011 and S&P Regional Banks Select Industry Index thereafter.

interpretation: Reduced co-movement has persisted for months and survives aggressive trimming. Broad equity-market exposure is an important descriptive dimension; simple rate-beta differences are insufficient as a complete explanation. No direction-of-return forecast follows.
scope: Archived at Will-established KRE destination. No canonical owner grade, trade approval or recurring monitoring rule changed.
